destination.title: Gravity and inflationary predictions
destination.question: How do nonminimal couplings, alternative gravitational formulations and modified expansion laws change the existence and observable predictions of inflation?
destination.summary: Compare gravitational constructions while retaining their different actions, scalar content, regimes and observational benchmarks.

targets: Dependence on coupling functions and gravitational formulation
regimes: Source-specific slow-roll, dissipative and full-background analyses
assumptions: Each gravitational construction is assessed within its stated model
Observational compatibility is source-dated and not presumed
conventions: Metric, Palatini and hybrid formulations remain distinct
A coupling to the Gauss–Bonnet invariant does not imply an additional Higgs–Ricci coupling
includes: Modified expansion laws without a shared microscopic origin
excludes: An inference of ultraviolet completion from a successful spectrum

sources.title: The Standard Model Higgs boson as the inflaton

evidence.text: Can the Standard Model Higgs drive inflation and generate acceptable primordial perturbations through a non-minimal gravitational coupling, without introducing an additional inflaton particle?

sources.title: Cosmic inflation from broken conformal symmetry

evidence.text: Can an asymptotically flat inflationary potential emerge from Palatini quadratic gravity by appropriately breaking local conformal symmetry in matter kinetic and effective potential terms, without imposing an additional global symmetry?

sources.title: Further Refining Swampland Conjecture on Inflation in General Scalar-Tensor Theories of Gravity

evidence.text: How does a phenomenological power-law correction modify nonminimally coupled quartic inflation and its potential-derivative constraints?

sources.title: Swampland conjectures in hybrid metric-Palatini gravity

evidence.text: The hybrid action retains metric curvature R while adding f(𝓡), where 𝓡 is built from an independent connection. The construction supplies the modified gravitational dynamics used for the inflationary application.

sources.title: Non-minimally coupled Natural Inflation: Palatini and Metric formalism with the recent BICEP/Keck

evidence.text: How does a polynomial nonminimal inflaton–curvature coupling change natural-inflation predictions for ns, r and α in Metric and Palatini formulations, and which sampled parameters agree with the BICEP/Keck contours used in this 2022 paper under specified reheating histories?

sources.title: Chaplygin inflation

evidence.text: Can a phenomenological modification of gravity inspired by the Chaplygin density law accommodate chaotic inflation, and which Chaplygin and inflaton scales satisfy the paper's CMB constraints? The authors aim to identify required assumptions and extrapolations rather than establish superiority over conventional inflation.

sources.title: Chaotic inflation on the brane

evidence.text: How does the minimal high-energy modification of gravity on a stable three-brane change slow-roll inflation and primordial perturbations, and can quadratic chaotic inflation occur below the four-dimensional Planck scale?

sources.title: Disentangling the $f(R)$ - Duality

evidence.text: How do decaying exponentials, rising exponentials, and monomial deformations of inflationary plateaus change their f(R) descriptions, including asymptotic powers, closed-form reconstructibility, and observable inflationary behavior?

sources.title: Gauss-Bonnet Inflation

evidence.text: Can a scalar coupled to the Gauss–Bonnet invariant generate early de Sitter expansion and an exit without an imposed scalar self-potential, after neglecting the Einstein–Hilbert term in a proposed strong-gravity regime?

sources.title: $\alpha$-attractor from superconformal E-models in brane inflation

evidence.text: Do superconformal E-model potentials retain inflationary attractors in Randall–Sundrum II brane cosmology, and how do brane corrections affect ns, r, parameter degeneracies and sub-Planckian field excursions?

sources.title: A note on supergravity inflation in braneworld

evidence.text: Can supergravity-motivated power-law potentials with exponential suppression yield observationally compatible inflation and sub-Planckian field excursions when embedded phenomenologically in braneworld cosmology?

sources.title: Logarithmic corrected $f(R)$ gravitational model and swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Determine whether corrected f(R) inflation can accommodate the paper's conjectured quantum-gravity restrictions and reported cosmological information, and whether those requirements constrain the curvature exponent and correction coefficients.

sources.title: Swampland implications of GW170817-compatible Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity

evidence.text: The setting describes inflation driven by one canonical scalar coupled to the Gauss–Bonnet invariant. This interaction changes homogeneous evolution and cosmological perturbation propagation and normalization.

sources.title: CMB from a Gauss-Bonnet-induced de Sitter fixed point

evidence.text: Can de Sitter fixed points sustained by a balance between a massive scalar potential and a scalar-dependent Gauss-Bonnet coupling generate CMB-compatible fluctuations, and thereby constrain the coupling function?

sources.title: Swampland conjectures in hybrid metric-Palatini gravity

evidence.text: The potential family tests whether changing the exponent away from the previously discussed quadratic case can improve simultaneous inflationary and swampland compatibility in the hybrid model.

sources.title: Swampland conjectures in hybrid metric-Palatini gravity

evidence.text: Does a power-law-potential realization of hybrid metric-Palatini inflation admit a common regime satisfying cosmological observations and the paper's de Sitter swampland inequalities? The proposed test uses ns, r, and potential-derivative ratios.

sources.title: Constraints on cosmological parameters in light of the scalar–tensor theory of gravity and swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Can power-law, exponential and logarithmic inflationary models in nonminimally coupled scalar–tensor gravity satisfy the paper's de Sitter swampland conditions while producing cosmological parameters compatible with its observational benchmarks?

sources.title: Swampland dS conjecture in mimetic $f(R, T)$ gravity

evidence.text: Can reconstructed inflationary histories in mimetic f(R,T)=R+δT gravity satisfy observational constraints and refined or further-refined de Sitter swampland criteria?

sources.title: Further Refining Swampland dS Conjecture in Mimetic f(G) Gravity

evidence.text: Can a reconstructed slow-roll inflation model in mimetic f(G) gravity match the paper's observational benchmarks while satisfying the refined or further refined de Sitter swampland conjecture?

sources.title: Swampland Criteria and Constraints on Inflation in a $f(R,T)$ Gravity Theory

evidence.text: Can canonical-scalar inflation in the specified linear f(R,T) model satisfy the paper's Planck 2018 cuts together with its implementation of swampland criteria, and which potential parameters permit overlap?

sources.title: Theory of gravity with nonminimal matter-nonmetricity coupling and the de-Sitter swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Can nonminimal matter–nonmetricity coupling reconcile single-scalar slow-roll inflation with the de Sitter swampland criteria?

sources.title: The de Sitter Swampland Conjectures in the Context of Chaplygin-Inspired Inflation

evidence.text: Can generalized Chaplygin-inspired single-field inflation satisfy the de Sitter swampland conditions, and how do these conditions further restrict inflationary potentials already constrained by CMB comparisons?

sources.title: Swampland diagnostics and observational tests of the inflationary universe in the Palatini formalism

evidence.text: How do the potential exponent and assumed inflationary duration affect CMB predictions and five distinct swampland diagnostics in an inherited quadratic Palatini model of quintessential inflation?

sources.title: The Standard Model Higgs boson as the inflaton

evidence.text: The analysis uses Einstein-frame potential slow-roll parameters, the e-fold integral and the COBE normalization U/ε=(0.027MP)⁴. The authors state that the same inflationary results can be obtained in the Jordan frame.

sources.title: Disentangling the $f(R)$ - Duality

evidence.text: Weyl transformation gives V=(f′R−f)/(2f′²). Reconstruction substitutes f′=exp(κφ), differentiates the resulting equation to solve for f′, and integrates; the original undifferentiated equation fixes the lost integration constant.

sources.title: Gauss-Bonnet Inflation

evidence.text: For f=λφ² in the Ricci-free model, the authors reduce the system to a Hubble evolution equation and integrate it for k=0. The relation φ²ȧ⁵=C0 is used to determine the scalar evolution, and a recursive Hubble-parameter hierarchy characterizes departure from inflation.

sources.title: $\alpha$-attractor from superconformal E-models in brane inflation

evidence.text: Numerical ns and r predictions are compared with the analytic approximations and scanned over α and V0/λ. Additional n values are examined. Later parameter plots use N=60 and the historical Planck 2018 and BICEP2/Keck constraints cited by the paper.

sources.title: A note on supergravity inflation in braneworld

evidence.text: Numerical slow-roll predictions use the modified e-fold integral N=−∫(YV/V′)dϕ, with Y=1+V/(2λ), and the scalar and tensor spectra appropriate to RSII. The authors report ending inflation at ε=1 because |η| is smaller at the exit point.

sources.title: Logarithmic corrected $f(R)$ gravitational model and swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Differentiate f, introduce its conjugate scalar, invert curvature on a valid branch, rescale the metric and normalize the kinetic term. Maintain the distinction between full f and its correction F.

sources.title: Palatini Higgs inflation and the refined dS conjecture

evidence.text: The setting isolates how an independently varied gravitational connection changes the canonical Higgs inflation potential and its refined-dS diagnostics. The analysis keeps a single scalar and freezes the non-minimal coupling xi.

sources.title: Induced Multi-phase Inflation with Reheating: Leptogenesis and Dark Matter Production in Metric versus Palatini

evidence.text: How do metric and Palatini gravity change the connection between non-minimal scalar inflation, radiatively stable reheating, decay-produced fermionic dark matter and Type-I-seesaw non-thermal leptogenesis?

sources.title: Gauss–Bonnet Inflation and the String Swampland

evidence.text: Do the adopted quantum-gravity conjectures point toward a particular curvature coupling in inflation?

sources.title: Two-Field quintessential Higgs Inflation

evidence.text: The model asks whether a nonminimally coupled Higgs can drive inflation while an exponentially coupled second scalar remains available for late dark energy.

sources.title: Non-Minimal M-flation

evidence.text: Can nonminimal coupling to gravity improve matrix inflation's observational predictions, reduce the required D3-brane multiplicity, enable spectator preheating and alleviate excursions beyond the proposed UV cutoff?

sources.title: Supergravity based inflation models: a review

evidence.text: How can supergravity inflation evade Hubble-scale inflaton masses and the exponential obstruction to large fields? The review presents representative models and extends the discussion to nonminimal Higgs inflation.

sources.title: Evading the Swampland de Sitter Obstruction via Thermodynamic Duality-Induced Horizon Corrections in Unimodular Gravity

evidence.text: Can quantum corrections to apparent-horizon entropy produce inflationary attractors in unimodular gravity with power-law nonlinear electrodynamics, while satisfying de Sitter and Distance conjectures and providing sufficient inflation?

sources.title: Swampland conjectures through ACT observations: Observational signatures of radiative-corrected inflation

evidence.text: Can radiatively corrected inflation simultaneously satisfy the paper's ACT/Planck/BAO observational benchmarks and the FRDSSC, SWGC, and SSWGC? The comparison concerns non-minimal Higgs inflation and a scalar-inflaton model with additional scalar and fermion sectors.

sources.title: Primordial black holes in non-minimal Gauss–Bonnet inflation in light of the PTA data

evidence.text: Can a two-part inflaton–Gauss–Bonnet coupling make monomial inflation compatible with CMB constraints while enhancing small-scale curvature perturbations enough for PBHs and scalar-induced gravitational waves, including a possible PTA signal?

sources.title: Inflationary dynamics of non-minimally coupled f(R) matter-curvature theories

evidence.text: Can power-law nonminimal matter-curvature couplings support stable inflation, how do their full background dynamics change CMB predictions, and can they resolve the graceful-exit problem of old inflation?

sources.title: Warm inflation in Weyl geometric gravity

evidence.text: Can matter-coupled Weyl R̃² gravity support dissipative inflation with a natural transition to radiation domination, and produce scalar/tensor observables compatible with the observational bounds adopted by the authors?

sources.title: Higgs Inflation and the Refined dS Conjecture

evidence.text: The model identifies the Standard Model Higgs with the inflaton by coupling its radial field nonminimally to curvature. The analysis asks whether the resulting Einstein-frame potential obeys the refined de Sitter inequalities.

sources.title: Higgs-modular inflation

evidence.text: How does a Higgs field carrying modular weight alter modular-inflation trajectories, observables, cutoff estimates, and reheating when it also couples nonminimally to gravity?

sources.title: Logarithmic corrected $f(R)$ gravitational model and swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Use curvature corrections to describe inflation and assess whether their parameters can accommodate cosmological information and the paper's proposed quantum-gravity restrictions.

sources.title: Non-minimal unimodular inflation revisited: Swampland diagnostics and CMB constraints

evidence.text: Can minimal non-minimal unimodular inflation simultaneously reproduce CMB observables, support a controlled 50–60 e-fold history with a standard exit, and satisfy FRDSSC, SWGC and SSWGC?

sources.title: Two-Field quintessential Higgs Inflation

evidence.text: Can a Higgs inflaton coexist with exponentially coupled quintessence while meeting CMB constraints, electroweak-vacuum stability requirements, and a proposed order-one potential-gradient bound?

sources.title: Implications of Palatini gravity for inflation and beyond

evidence.text: How does treating the metric and connection independently change inflationary predictions, reheating, and models connecting inflation to late-time acceleration when non-minimal couplings or higher-curvature terms are present?

sources.title: Two scalar fields inflation from scale-invariant gravity with modified measure

evidence.text: Can globally scale-invariant gravity with an independent integration measure naturally generate two scalar degrees of freedom, inflation and a small positive final vacuum energy in the second-order formalism?

sources.title: Non-minimal Higgs inflation in the context of warm scenario in the light of Planck data

evidence.text: Can non-minimal Higgs inflation, treated as warm inflation with dissipation Γ=Γ0T, produce scalar tilt, tensor fraction and running compatible with the Planck constraints used in the paper?

sources.title: Revisiting Scalar Tensor inflation by swampland criteria and Reheating

evidence.text: Which choices of potential and gravitational coupling permit the paper's joint inflationary selection? Three independent ansatzes probe power-law dependence, a quadratic potential with a polynomial coupling, and simultaneous exponential dependence.

destination.title: Constructing and protecting inflationary potentials
destination.question: How can inflationary potentials be realized, flattened and stabilized in supergravity or other stated scalar constructions, and how sensitive are they to couplings and corrections?
destination.summary: Separate supergravity obstructions, spectator stabilization, protected hybrid constructions and phenomenological flat potentials while providing a common construction question.

assumptions: Supergravity is one setting, not a requirement for every construction
Proposed protection mechanisms require their own assumptions
conventions: Potential-flatness tuning is distinguished from inflationary-scale normalization
includes: The supergravity mass and exponential obstructions
Construction and stabilization as distinguishable targets
excludes: Identification of every flat potential with Starobinsky inflation

evidence.text: How sensitively do supergravity inflation models depend on relative couplings, and can small departures from their Starobinsky or new-inflation limits improve CMB agreement while alleviating large-field initial-condition problems? The focus is potential-flatness tuning rather than the overall inflationary hierarchy.

sources.title: On hybrid monodromy inflation — hic sunt dracones

evidence.text: Can Stewart-type two-field hybrid inflation fit CMB constraints with sub-Planckian excursions while remaining stable against field-theory and quantum-gravity corrections, and can a massive-form realization supply the required protection?

sources.title: Starobinsky-like Inflationary Models as Avatars of No-Scale Supergravity

evidence.text: Which no-scale supergravity models reproduce the Starobinsky inflationary potential, how can their spectator fields be stabilized, and which generalizations change the CMB predictions?

destination.title: Starobinsky origins and deformations
destination.question: How is Starobinsky-like inflation realized or modified in the stated constructions, and what changes follow for observables, consistency conditions and initial-field sensitivity?
destination.summary: Keep supergravity realizations, altered curvature powers, species-induced corrections, quartic-curvature terms and Genesis-induced deformations distinct.

regimes: Exact Starobinsky limits and source-defined departures
assumptions: A common limiting potential does not establish common microscopic origin
A general f(R) action need not be a controlled perturbation of Starobinsky inflation
conventions: Keep coupling deformations, curvature corrections and inverse-e-fold expansions distinct
includes: Stable-transition questions when they alter the inflationary stage
